youtube.baslik: How is an audiometer checked each morning before the first patient? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: The biological check takes about five minutes at the start of each test day: cables and earphones are checked first by eye, then by listening. In common practice, a 10 dB or greater change in a normal-hearing tester's own thresholds calls for an acoustic calibration check.

sahneler.alt: If it persists, _the device is not used_
cumleler: The biological check takes about five minutes before the first patient.
First, cables, plugs and earphone cushions are inspected by eye.
Then each tone is heard as clean and from the right channel.
A normal-hearing tester measures their own thresholds against a stored baseline.
Commonly, a change of ten decibels or more needs an acoustic check.
